paracetamol_acetaminophen.common_uses: Mild to moderate pain and fever.
paracetamol_acetaminophen.dosage_adult: 500-1000 mg orally every 4-6 hours as needed; max 4000 mg/day (often 3000 mg/day in outpatient use).
major_interactions: Warfarin (chronic high-dose use can increase INR and bleeding risk)
paracetamol_acetaminophen.warnings: Overdose can cause life-threatening liver failure; account for acetaminophen in combination products.

ibuprofen.dosage_adult: 200-400 mg orally every 6-8 hours as needed; max 1200 mg/day OTC or 3200 mg/day under supervision.
major_interactions: ACE inhibitors/ARBs plus diuretics (acute kidney injury risk)
Other NSAIDs (additive GI and renal toxicity)
contraindications: Active peptic ulcer disease or GI bleeding
ibuprofen.warnings: Can cause GI bleeding, kidney injury, fluid retention, and increased cardiovascular risk.

aspirin.common_uses: Pain, fever, inflammatory conditions, antiplatelet therapy.
aspirin.dosage_adult: Analgesia: 325-650 mg every 4-6 hours; antiplatelet: 75-162 mg once daily.
major_interactions: Ibuprofen (may reduce antiplatelet effect if timed poorly)
contraindications: Children/adolescents with viral illness (Reye syndrome risk)
aspirin.warnings: Risk of GI bleeding and hemorrhagic stroke; avoid in children with viral infections.

amoxicillin.common_uses: Susceptible bacterial respiratory, ENT, skin, and urinary infections.
amoxicillin.dosage_adult: 500 mg every 8 hours or 875 mg every 12 hours orally, depending on infection severity.
amoxicillin.warnings: Rash is common in infectious mononucleosis; monitor for anaphylaxis in penicillin-allergic patients.

metformin.common_uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus and insulin resistance.
metformin.dosage_adult: Start 500 mg once or twice daily with meals; typical maintenance 1500-2000 mg/day.
major_interactions: Iodinated contrast (lactic acidosis risk in renal dysfunction)
metformin.warnings: Lactic acidosis is rare but serious; pause around contrast studies per renal function guidance.

major_interactions: Simvastatin (limit simvastatin dose due to myopathy risk)
amlodipine.warnings: May cause peripheral edema, flushing, dizziness, and reflex tachycardia.

omeprazole.common_uses: GERD, peptic ulcer disease, H. pylori regimens, upper GI bleed prophylaxis.
omeprazole.dosage_adult: 20-40 mg orally once daily before meals.
omeprazole.warnings: Long-term use may increase risk of hypomagnesemia, fractures, C. difficile, and B12 deficiency.

metoprolol.common_uses: Hypertension, angina, rate control, heart failure (succinate form), post-MI therapy.
metoprolol.dosage_adult: Tartrate 25-100 mg twice daily or succinate 25-200 mg once daily depending on indication.
major_interactions: CYP2D6 inhibitors such as fluoxetine/paroxetine (increased metoprolol levels)
contraindications: Second- or third-degree AV block without pacemaker
metoprolol.warnings: Do not stop abruptly due to rebound tachycardia/ischemia; may mask hypoglycemia.

losartan.common_uses: Hypertension, diabetic nephropathy, and cardiovascular risk reduction.
losartan.dosage_adult: 25-100 mg orally once daily or divided twice daily.
major_interactions: NSAIDs (may reduce antihypertensive effect and worsen renal function)
losartan.warnings: Monitor renal function and potassium; can cause hypotension and renal impairment.

atorvastatin.common_uses: Hyperlipidemia and prevention of cardiovascular events.
major_interactions: Large amounts of grapefruit juice (increased statin exposure)
atorvastatin.warnings: Check for muscle pain/weakness and liver injury signs; monitor liver enzymes as indicated.

contraindications: Hypersensitivity to cetirizine, hydroxyzine, or levocetirizine
cetirizine.warnings: Usually low sedation risk, but drowsiness can occur; caution when driving.

azithromycin.common_uses: Respiratory, skin, and selected sexually transmitted infections.
azithromycin.dosage_adult: 500 mg on day 1 then 250 mg daily on days 2-5 for many respiratory infections.
major_interactions: Aluminum/magnesium antacids (reduced absorption if taken together)
contraindications: History of cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction with azithromycin
azithromycin.warnings: Risk of QT prolongation and torsades de pointes, especially in high-risk patients.

ciprofloxacin.common_uses: Complicated urinary, GI, bone, and selected gram-negative infections.
ciprofloxacin.dosage_adult: 250-750 mg orally every 12 hours depending on infection.
major_interactions: Antacids, iron, calcium, zinc (markedly reduce absorption)
ciprofloxacin.warnings: Can cause tendinopathy, neuropathy, CNS effects, dysglycemia, and aortic aneurysm risk in susceptible patients.

doxycycline.common_uses: Respiratory and skin infections, atypical organisms, tick-borne infections, malaria prophylaxis.
doxycycline.dosage_adult: 100 mg orally every 12 hours on day 1, then 100 mg once or twice daily.
doxycycline.warnings: Avoid routine use in children under 8 years unless benefits outweigh risks; photosensitivity is common.

prednisolone.common_uses: Inflammatory and autoimmune disorders, asthma exacerbations, allergic reactions.
prednisolone.dosage_adult: 5-60 mg orally daily depending on condition; taper when prolonged therapy is stopped.
major_interactions: Live vaccines (infection risk with immunosuppressive doses)
prednisolone.warnings: Long-term use may cause adrenal suppression, hyperglycemia, osteoporosis, infection risk, and mood changes.

salbutamol_albuterol.common_uses: Relief of acute bronchospasm in asthma and COPD.
salbutamol_albuterol.dosage_adult: Inhaler: 1-2 puffs (90 mcg each) every 4-6 hours as needed.
major_interactions: MAO inhibitors and tricyclic antidepressants (potentiate cardiovascular effects)
salbutamol_albuterol.warnings: May cause tachycardia, tremor, and hypokalemia; frequent rescue use signals poor control.

insulin.common_uses: Type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes, hyperglycemic emergencies.
insulin.dosage_adult: Individualized; common basal start in type 2 diabetes is 0.1-0.2 units/kg/day.
insulin.warnings: Monitor glucose closely; dosing errors can cause severe hypo- or hyperglycemia.

diclofenac.common_uses: Musculoskeletal pain, arthritis, acute inflammatory pain.
diclofenac.dosage_adult: 50 mg orally 2-3 times daily; usual max 150 mg/day (oral formulations).
major_interactions: ACE inhibitors/ARBs and diuretics (renal injury risk)
diclofenac.warnings: Increased risk of cardiovascular thrombotic events and GI bleeding.

ranitidine.common_uses: Historically used for acid reflux and ulcer disease.
ranitidine.dosage_adult: Historical dosing: 150 mg orally twice daily.
major_interactions: Drugs requiring acidic gastric pH (reduced absorption)
ranitidine.warnings: Withdrawn/restricted in many countries because of NDMA impurity concerns; use current local guidance.

oral_rehydration_salts.common_uses: Treatment and prevention of dehydration from diarrhea and vomiting.
oral_rehydration_salts.dosage_adult: Frequent small volumes; commonly 200-250 mL after each loose stool, adjusted to thirst and losses.
major_interactions: Use caution with severe renal failure due to electrolyte load
contraindications: Severe dehydration requiring immediate IV resuscitation
oral_rehydration_salts.warnings: Use correctly prepared solution; incorrect dilution can cause electrolyte disturbances.

chloroquine.common_uses: Malaria treatment/prophylaxis in susceptible regions and some autoimmune diseases.
chloroquine.dosage_adult: For sensitive malaria, common total adult treatment dose is 2.5 g chloroquine phosphate over 3 days.
contraindications: Retinal or visual field changes attributable to 4-aminoquinolines
chloroquine.warnings: Monitor for retinopathy and cardiotoxicity with prolonged/high-dose use.

artemisinin_based_combination.common_uses: First-line treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in many regions.
artemisinin_based_combination.dosage_adult: Artemether/lumefantrine 20/120 mg: 4 tablets at 0, 8, 24, 36, 48, and 60 hours with food.
contraindications: Use caution/alternative regimens in severe malaria
artemisinin_based_combination.warnings: Take with fatty food or milk to improve absorption; monitor QT risk in susceptible patients.

albendazole.dosage_adult: Many intestinal helminths: 400 mg orally once; longer regimens for tissue infections.
major_interactions: Cimetidine and praziquantel (increase active metabolite levels)
albendazole.warnings: Monitor liver enzymes and blood counts with prolonged therapy.

mebendazole.common_uses: Pinworm, roundworm, whipworm, and hookworm infections.
mebendazole.dosage_adult: 100 mg orally twice daily for 3 days or single-dose regimens depending on parasite.
mebendazole.warnings: Avoid use in early pregnancy unless clearly needed.

ferrous_sulfate.common_uses: Prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anemia.
ferrous_sulfate.dosage_adult: 325 mg tablet (about 65 mg elemental iron) once to three times daily depending on tolerance and need.
contraindications: Anemias not due to iron deficiency
ferrous_sulfate.warnings: Keep away from children; accidental overdose can be fatal.

folic_acid.common_uses: Folate deficiency, megaloblastic anemia due to folate deficiency, neural tube defect prevention.
folic_acid.dosage_adult: 0.4-1 mg orally daily for supplementation; often 1 mg daily for deficiency.
contraindications: Untreated vitamin B12 deficiency without concurrent B12 therapy
folic_acid.warnings: Can mask hematologic signs of B12 deficiency while neurologic injury progresses.

vitamin_a.common_uses: Vitamin A deficiency and deficiency-related eye/immune complications.
vitamin_a.dosage_adult: Typical maintenance supplementation around 5000 IU daily; high-dose regimens are indication-specific.
major_interactions: Warfarin (high-dose vitamin A may increase bleeding risk)
vitamin_a.warnings: Excess intake causes hepatotoxicity, bone toxicity, and teratogenicity.

zinc_supplements.common_uses: Zinc deficiency and adjunct treatment in diarrhea.
zinc_supplements.dosage_adult: 20-40 mg elemental zinc daily, adjusted by indication.
major_interactions: Tetracyclines and fluoroquinolones (chelation reduces antibiotic absorption)
Iron and calcium at same time (reduced zinc absorption)
zinc_supplements.warnings: Long-term high-dose use can cause copper deficiency and anemia.

cotrimoxazole.common_uses: Urinary, respiratory, GI, skin infections and opportunistic infection prophylaxis/treatment.
cotrimoxazole.dosage_adult: 160/800 mg orally every 12 hours for many infections.
contraindications: Megaloblastic anemia due to folate deficiency
cotrimoxazole.warnings: Can cause severe skin reactions (SJS/TEN), marrow suppression, hyperkalemia, and renal effects.

gentamicin.common_uses: Severe gram-negative infections and synergy in select serious infections.
gentamicin.dosage_adult: Typically 5-7 mg/kg IV once daily (extended-interval) with renal adjustment.
major_interactions: Other nephrotoxic drugs such as vancomycin (renal toxicity)
contraindications: Myasthenia gravis (relative; risk of neuromuscular blockade)
gentamicin.warnings: Monitor drug levels, renal function, and hearing due to nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity.

cloxacillin.common_uses: Methicillin-susceptible staphylococcal skin and soft tissue infections.
cloxacillin.dosage_adult: 250-500 mg orally every 6 hours on an empty stomach; IV dosing for severe infection.
cloxacillin.warnings: Monitor for hypersensitivity and antibiotic-associated diarrhea.

phenytoin.common_uses: Focal and generalized tonic-clonic seizures; status epilepticus maintenance.
phenytoin.dosage_adult: Common maintenance is 300-400 mg/day orally in divided doses, adjusted by levels.
contraindications: Sinus bradycardia, sinoatrial block, second/third-degree AV block (especially IV use)
phenytoin.warnings: Narrow therapeutic index; monitor serum levels and for serious rash, hepatotoxicity, and blood dyscrasias.

carbamazepine.common_uses: Focal seizures, trigeminal neuralgia, bipolar disorder.
carbamazepine.dosage_adult: Start around 200 mg twice daily and titrate to effect and serum levels.
major_interactions: Warfarin and oral contraceptives (reduced concentrations via enzyme induction)
contraindications: Concomitant MAOI use or within 14 days
Known HLA-B*1502 risk populations without testing (for severe rash risk)
carbamazepine.warnings: Risk of SJS/TEN, aplastic anemia, agranulocytosis, and hyponatremia.

diazepam.common_uses: Anxiety, status epilepticus adjunct, muscle spasm, alcohol withdrawal.
diazepam.dosage_adult: 2-10 mg orally 2-4 times daily depending on indication; acute IV dosing for emergencies.
diazepam.warnings: Risk of dependence, withdrawal, oversedation, falls, and respiratory depression.

morphine.common_uses: Moderate to severe acute and chronic pain.
morphine.dosage_adult: Opioid-naive oral immediate-release often starts around 5-15 mg every 4 hours as needed.
major_interactions: Benzodiazepines and other CNS depressants (respiratory depression)
contraindications: Acute/severe bronchial asthma in unmonitored settings
Known or suspected GI obstruction including paralytic ileus
morphine.warnings: High risk of dependence, overdose, and fatal respiratory depression; use lowest effective dose.

lidocaine.category: local anesthetic and class Ib antiarrhythmic
lidocaine.common_uses: Local anesthesia, ventricular arrhythmias (IV), topical pain relief.
lidocaine.dosage_adult: Local infiltration typically up to 4.5 mg/kg (without epinephrine), not exceeding maximum recommended dose.
major_interactions: Cimetidine and beta blockers (reduced lidocaine clearance)
contraindications: Severe SA/AV/intraventricular block without pacemaker (systemic use)
lidocaine.warnings: Systemic toxicity can cause seizures, arrhythmias, and cardiovascular collapse.

epinephrine.common_uses: Anaphylaxis, cardiac arrest, severe bronchospasm, refractory hypotension.
epinephrine.dosage_adult: Anaphylaxis: 0.3-0.5 mg IM (1 mg/mL) every 5-15 minutes as needed.
epinephrine.warnings: In emergencies, epinephrine is life-saving; dosing errors and IV bolus misuse can cause severe adverse effects.

atropine.common_uses: Symptomatic bradycardia, organophosphate poisoning, reduction of secretions.
atropine.dosage_adult: Bradycardia: 0.5 mg IV every 3-5 minutes to max 3 mg.
major_interactions: Oral potassium chloride tablets (GI injury risk)
contraindications: GI obstructive disease or paralytic ileus
atropine.warnings: Can cause delirium, urinary retention, hyperthermia, and tachyarrhythmias, especially in older adults.

oxytocin.common_uses: Labor induction/augmentation and prevention or treatment of postpartum hemorrhage.
oxytocin.dosage_adult: Labor induction often starts at 1-2 milliunits/min IV infusion, titrated to uterine response.
major_interactions: Vasoconstrictors with regional anesthesia (severe hypertension risk)
contraindications: Fetal distress when delivery is not imminent
oxytocin.warnings: Requires continuous maternal-fetal monitoring due to risk of uterine rupture and fetal compromise.

misoprostol.common_uses: Medical abortion, cervical ripening, labor induction, postpartum hemorrhage treatment, NSAID-ulcer prevention.
misoprostol.dosage_adult: Ulcer prevention: 200 mcg orally four times daily; obstetric dosing varies by protocol.
contraindications: Pregnancy when used for ulcer prevention
misoprostol.warnings: Causes uterine contractions and can induce abortion; use only under appropriate protocol.

magnesium_sulfate.common_uses: Prevention/treatment of eclamptic seizures, severe hypomagnesemia, selected arrhythmias.
magnesium_sulfate.dosage_adult: Eclampsia regimen often 4-6 g IV loading dose, then 1-2 g/hour infusion.
major_interactions: Calcium channel blockers (hypotension and neuromuscular blockade risk)
magnesium_sulfate.warnings: Monitor reflexes, respiratory rate, urine output, and serum magnesium to avoid toxicity.

furosemide.common_uses: Edema from heart/liver/kidney disease and hypertension.
furosemide.dosage_adult: 20-80 mg orally once or twice daily; adjust to clinical response.
furosemide.warnings: Can cause volume depletion, hypotension, hypokalemia, and kidney dysfunction.

hydrochlorothiazide.dosage_adult: 12.5-25 mg orally once daily for hypertension; higher doses for edema as needed.
hydrochlorothiazide.warnings: May cause hyponatremia, hypokalemia, hyperuricemia, and glucose intolerance.

enalapril.common_uses: Hypertension, heart failure, and kidney protection in selected patients.
enalapril.dosage_adult: 5-20 mg/day orally in 1-2 divided doses, titrated to response.
enalapril.warnings: Can cause cough, hyperkalemia, kidney injury, and potentially life-threatening angioedema.

nifedipine.common_uses: Hypertension, angina, and selected obstetric tocolysis protocols.
nifedipine.dosage_adult: Extended-release 30-60 mg orally once daily; titrate as needed.
major_interactions: Other antihypertensives including beta blockers (additive hypotension)
nifedipine.warnings: Immediate-release forms can cause rapid hypotension and reflex tachycardia; use appropriate formulation.

warfarin.common_uses: Prevention and treatment of thromboembolism and stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation.
warfarin.dosage_adult: Usually start 2-5 mg orally daily and titrate to target INR (often 2.0-3.0).
major_interactions: TMP-SMX, metronidazole, amiodarone, azoles, many antibiotics (INR increase)
contraindications: Recent hemorrhagic stroke or high bleeding-risk situations
warfarin.warnings: Requires regular INR monitoring; many food and drug interactions can cause severe bleeding or thrombosis.

heparin.common_uses: VTE prophylaxis/treatment, acute coronary syndromes, bridging anticoagulation.
heparin.dosage_adult: Treatment often starts with 80 units/kg IV bolus then 18 units/kg/hour infusion, adjusted by aPTT/anti-Xa.
major_interactions: Thrombolytics and other anticoagulants (major bleeding risk)
heparin.warnings: Monitor platelets and coagulation; watch for HIT and bleeding complications.

dexamethasone.common_uses: Severe inflammation, cerebral edema, antiemesis, croup, and other steroid-responsive conditions.
dexamethasone.dosage_adult: 0.5-10 mg/day orally or parenterally depending on indication.
major_interactions: Live vaccines (infection risk with immunosuppressive doses)
dexamethasone.warnings: Long-term therapy risks include adrenal suppression, hyperglycemia, infections, osteoporosis, and psychiatric effects.

hydrocortisone.common_uses: Adrenal insufficiency replacement, inflammatory disorders, allergic and dermatologic conditions.
hydrocortisone.dosage_adult: Adrenal replacement often totals 15-25 mg/day orally in divided doses; higher doses for acute illness.
hydrocortisone.warnings: Abrupt discontinuation after prolonged use can precipitate adrenal crisis; taper appropriately.

chlorhexidine.common_uses: Skin antisepsis before procedures, oral gingivitis rinse, wound cleansing.
chlorhexidine.dosage_adult: Oral rinse 0.12%: 15 mL swish for 30 seconds twice daily; topical strengths vary by use.
major_interactions: Anionic compounds/soaps can reduce antiseptic activity
Concurrent irritating topical agents can increase local irritation
chlorhexidine.warnings: Rare but severe allergic reactions can occur; avoid contact with meninges and middle ear.
